raw: {"analysis": "Both responses provide solid plans addressing the core requirements: verification/delay mechanisms, handling of the flaky check, immutable schema, SSL rotation, dual approval, and cost constraints. HFB is more granular with explicit gates (G0-G9), including a simulation step to replay historical maintenance data to prove zero false alarms, and a post-deploy monitoring step for SSL rotation. It also clearly separates lanes and includes a risk note about CI time and cost. NXF is also strong, with a shadow mode test and a retraction entry for immutable logs, but it lacks the same level of detail in gate structure and post-deploy verification. HFB's plan is more actionable and leaves fewer open questions for the requester.", "verdict": "HFB"}
